title: Independent ideas. Extraordinary finds.
intro: A daily selection of independent games and useful Android apps, with original F7 insights and links to their creators.

entries.name: Blocks Beyond the Stars
entries.summary: A block-based 3D space crafting game built by a father and his ten-year-old, who is credited as lead product manager. You wake on your own ship, fly system-scale routes to procedurally generated planets, mine and craft, tame creatures, and build bases or whole ships block by block, solo or with friends on a self-hostable server.
features: 48 planet types across generated star systems, from gas giants with floating sky cities to bone deserts, plus one-off landmark worlds and rare two-way wormholes
Per-position weather and seasons with storms, acid rain and meteor showers that have real consequences, and a day/night terminator you can dress for
A bio lab that samples every species you harvest or defeat, identifies its effects, and lets you clone and cross plants and animals into new ones
Ships you lay keel by keel and keep growing during a spacewalk, planet bases with life-support fields, and monorail hover trains you can build
Movement kit of climbing, an energy rope to reel across gaps, a glider, hover speeders and boats, plus giants up to sixty blocks tall to survive
Persistent client/server multiplayer with a content filter, one-command reporting and per-player mute, aimed at family play
entries.insight: The design doc here is a child's imagination, and it shows in the small rules: bandits are chased off rather than killed, weapons default to tools, and every world wraps east-west so you can walk all the way around a planet. It is a rare open-source game where the safety design and the wonder design come from the same person.

entries.name: Ashfolk

price.label: Free to play in the browser, with an optional paid supporter tier

entries.summary: A god simulator that runs on WebGPU in your browser. You shape a seeded floating island, then watch its first tribes gather, hunt, farm and build their way from the Stone Age to the Iron Age while you decide what kind of weather they get.
features: Islands generated from a seed with rivers, lakes, waterfalls, swamps, biomes, seasons and snow
Tribes that expand, raid each other over land and later sign peace, with a chronicle you can read
Wildlife that the tribes share the island with: deer, mammoths, ibex, hares and wolf packs that hunt them
Powers ranging from a single meteor to lightning storms, tornado swarms, a black hole over a camp, or a mushroom cloud that leaves a crater
Land that heals: burnt ground grows back and craters fill into lakes
A short guided first island, plus worlds that save themselves in the browser
entries.insight: Most god games score you on population. Ashfolk's interesting mechanic is the fe ledger: tribes remember raids, negotiate peace, and keep growing whether or not you interfere, so the meteor is a comment on their story rather than the point of it.

entries.name: Operation Steel Tide
entries.summary: An open-source tactical FPS made in Godot 4.6 with C#, set in the Jianghai old-city port. Three modes share one build: a three-operator extraction run with AI squadmates, an independent 5v5 demolition match, and a training range where you choose bots, weapons and ammunition before you shoot. Downloads need no Godot or .NET install.
features: Extraction loop: pick a class and loadout, close the comms relay, download the cargo manifest, loot, then reach the green zone and board before the timer
Only loot above your deployment baseline is banked, so a bad run can genuinely cost you
Five operator classes with follow, hold and move orders, class skills, combat and revive behaviour, plus AI takeover when a co-op player drops
Separate 5v5 demolition with a buy phase, plant and defuse, side swap at half-time and overtime on a draw
A dedicated training range with configurable bot types, counts, weapons and ammo tiers, and bots that respawn automatically
entries.insight: Extraction shooters are almost always live services with inventory you buy back. Steel Tide keeps the same tension — bank only what beats your baseline — inside a plain downloadable MIT-licensed build, which makes the risk maths something you can read in the source.

entries.name: I Keep Having This Dream
entries.summary: A strategy roguelike where each cycle of a dream is a grid you escape by laying tiles. Staying longer makes the cycle more dangerous, so every detour toward an item is a bet against the enemies that get stronger near the exit.
features: Build a route tile by tile out of each dreamscape cycle, with danger rising the longer you linger
25+ upgradeable perks that push your strategy toward attack, defence or tempo
150+ collectible items and 100+ special enemies whose abilities can end a run if ignored
80+ one-off events offering a temporary boost when you take the detour
Persistent unlocks of enemies, events and cosmetics across several playthroughs
A C++ game core in a thin Java and SDL2 shell, building for arm64-v8a and armeabi-v7a on Android 5.0 and up
entries.insight: The clock here is attached to your own greed rather than a wave timer: the cycle only gets worse while you keep looting it, so the game is really about deciding when a route is finished.

entries.name: Astro Loop
entries.summary: A roguelike space shooter about surviving endless asteroid and enemy waves in a loop you were not meant to escape. One finger steers, the guns fire themselves, and difficulty keeps climbing so the only real decision is which upgrade you take next.
features: Single-finger steering with automatic weapons, built for one-handed play
Recruit a crew of pilots and unlock new ships between runs
Fresh weapon and upgrade choices every run against a difficulty curve that never stops rising
No internet permission at all: no ads, no tracking, and nothing leaves the phone
No camera, microphone, location, contacts, file or network permissions requested
Drawn as vectors on an Android Canvas in pure Kotlin, with no game engine
entries.insight: Astro Loop's constraint is the interesting part: with no network permission the whole roguelike has to live on the device, which is why it plays on a plane and why no progress can be held hostage by a server.

entries.name: Thank You for the Fish

price.label: Free, open-source, with an optional donation on itch.io

entries.summary: A tiny boat that sits in the corner of a Mac desktop and fishes while you work. It catches on its own, keeps a collection of 160 creatures, and takes breaks for you as well, so the game paces itself to a working day rather than demanding one.
features: 160 sea creatures including 10 legends, with four traits producing 640 possible appearances
Bite intervals you set anywhere from 1 to 120 minutes, so fishing matches your task length
Automatic breaks after a chosen number of catches
A draggable, resizable desktop boat with local saves that works offline after setup
A v0.5.1 art pass giving the 60 expansion creatures toy-like artwork, transparent edges and anatomy-specific motion
Interface defaults to Simplified Chinese, with an experimental partial English translation in Settings
entries.insight: The forced-break timer turns an idle game inside out: instead of asking for your attention, it is the reason you look away from the spreadsheet, which is a more honest use of a desktop pet.

entries.name: Trackhop
entries.summary: Trackhop keeps playlists identical across music services, on a schedule, from your phone. There is no Trackhop account and no Trackhop server: the sync runs on the device and access tokens never leave it.
features: Mirrors playlists across Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, TIDAL, Deezer, SoundCloud, LiveOne, Subsonic/Navidrome, Koel, Jellyfin, Emby, Plex, Lyrion and Mopidy
Reads sources from Last.fm, ListenBrainz, NetEase Cloud Music, QQ Music and JioSaavn links, and bridges anything else through CSV, TSV, M3U, iTunes XML, JSON or pasted text
Scheduled syncs with one shared list of tracks that could not be matched, reviewable before you act
Group playlists shared so each member keeps them on their own service, plus Discover pages that follow a playlist's artists for releases, concerts and setlists
Store builds use official APIs only; the free Trackhop Bridge plugin, and the GitHub and F-Droid builds, add quick sign-in routes for services without one
Desktop and Docker builds for running the same sync on a computer or server
entries.insight: Playlist migration tools normally ask you to hand your service tokens to their backend. Trackhop inverts that: the phone does the work and the tokens stay on it, which is the difference between a sync service and a sync you own.

entries.name: Fonte
entries.summary: A small open-source updater for apps you installed outside an app store. Give it a repository link and Fonte finds the latest release, picks the APK matching your phone, verifies it and installs it, with no trackers and no Google Play Services.
features: Sources include GitHub (private repositories too, with a token), self-hosted GitLab, Codeberg, Forgejo, Gitea, F-Droid, IzzyOnDroid and other F-Droid repositories
Chooses the build for your processor, with an optional regular-expression name filter and pre-releases if you want them
Background checks every 3, 6, 12 or 24 hours that wait for an unmetered network by default
Deliberately smaller attack surface than Obtainium: no native code, no WebView and no dynamic code loading, so it works with GrapheneOS dynamic-code-loading restrictions on
Imports your existing Obtainium app list, and checks all apps at once over HTTP/3 and HTTP/2 with not-modified responses for unchanged sources
entries.insight: Fonte describes itself as an Obtainium alternative with fewer features, and that framing is the point: an updater that installs other apps is the worst place to add a WebView, so the missing capabilities are the security model.

entries.name: AppDNS
entries.summary: AppDNS gives each Android app its own Private DNS (DNS-over-TLS) setting and switches it when you open that app. It writes directly to Android's built-in setting, so there is no VPN tunnel, no always-on notification and no drain on battery.
features: Per-app rules assigning any DNS profile to any app, with search and filters
Switching is event-driven rather than polled, landing in under 10 ms after an app opens
Built-in Cloudflare, AdGuard, Google and Quad9 profiles plus unlimited custom DoT hostnames such as NextDNS, Control D and Mullvad
Configurable exit behaviour: turn DNS off, restore your default, or keep it when you leave the app
A permission watchdog that warns you if a reboot or update silently disables a grant, and in-app updates with live download progress
About 2.3 MB, no analytics, and an accessibility service that reads only the foreground package name, never screen content; the one-time DNS permission is granted over ADB
entries.insight: Because it drives Android's own Private DNS setting instead of a local proxy, AppDNS can give your browser AdGuard's blocking while your real WireGuard or work VPN keeps working — per-app DNS without a second tunnel.

entries.name: TwinnDroid
entries.summary: TwinnDroid runs two or more copies of the same app, each with its own login, and can wall them into a sandbox. It uses no root and no virtualisation layer: every copy is a real app that Android itself keeps apart.
features: Clones an installed app, or an .apk, .apks, .xapk or .apkm file, with its own name and icon so Discord and Discord (Alt) sit side by side
An optional work-profile sandbox with separate storage, accounts and contacts, which also runs apps that refuse to be cloned
Hardening that stops a clone from seeing other apps or being reached by them, and keeps clones from being linked to each other
Permission stripping per copy, such as removing location or contacts
One-tap clone updates when the original app updates, without logging you out, plus APK extraction with splits included
Backup and restore for clones and settings, 23 languages with right-to-left layouts, and theming with Material You
entries.insight: Dual-app features usually fake a second space inside one process. TwinnDroid installs a genuinely separate signed package, which means the clone inherits Android's own isolation instead of trusting the cloner to enforce it.

entries.name: Fern
entries.summary: An offline Material You system monitor for Android that charts CPU, RAM, battery, thermals, storage and network in one dashboard, and stays useful without an account, an ad network or a tracker.
features: Live dashboard with smooth history charts for CPU, RAM, battery, storage and network
Details and peak views, including shareable metric snapshots
A process view with per-app CPU and RAM when you grant elevated access
An optional compact overlay, dynamic-island style, for temperature and memory
Advanced sampling through Shizuku (preferred) or root, with everything else working without either
Seed-colour theming with light, dark and system modes, plus an AMOLED-friendly dark theme
entries.insight: Fern splits its data honestly: the unprivileged view always works, and the per-app attribution that needs Shizuku or root is opt-in, so you can see exactly what you are trading for a more accurate reading.

entries.name: Relay
entries.summary: Relay shares your phone's internet — mobile data, Wi-Fi or its active VPN — with a Windows PC over one encrypted WireGuard tunnel, for every app on the PC and for both TCP and UDP. No root, no account and no relay server in the middle.
features: Three-step start: tap Start Sharing on the phone, pick the device or type the two digits it shows, then tap Allow
The phone runs a small WireGuard endpoint while the PC client routes the whole system through it
Pairs over the same Wi-Fi, the phone's hotspot, or a USB cable, offering to enable USB tethering for you
Fresh keys per pairing, an explicit approval before any computer gets in, and keys destroyed when sharing stops
A companion Windows client built alongside the Android app, both released from the same repository
entries.insight: Reverse tethering normally means a root hack or a paid utility that proxies your PC. Relay instead makes the phone the WireGuard endpoint, so the PC gets an ordinary encrypted tunnel to a device you already trust.

entries.name: AndCode

price.label: Free, open-source; bring your own agent accounts

entries.summary: A native Android GUI for coding agents: OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity, driven by touch instead of a terminal. The agents run on the phone itself inside a PRoot Linux environment, or remotely against your own OpenCode server. AndCode is an independent project and does not provide model access or subscriptions.
features: On-device runtime that installs Alpine Linux, Git, bash, curl, ripgrep and the agent CLIs automatically, with a Debian rootfs alongside for the glibc-linked Antigravity binary
An embedded real-PTY terminal with streamed output, stdin, Ctrl+C and colours, opening in the workspace you came from
Dev servers started in that terminal appear as chips that open the page in the in-app browser, and loopback previews can be pinned inside the conversation as live cards that reload as files change
Git status and diff review from the GUI, plus streaming tool execution with explicit approval requests
OAuth credentials for Antigravity stored only inside the Linux rootfs rather than Android preferences, and a live model catalog read from the signed-in instance
Remote mode connecting to an existing OpenCode server on your own PC, Mac or Linux machine
entries.insight: The distinction that matters is that AndCode installs the agent on the handset rather than streaming your desktop to it: a phone that carries its own git, shell and agent runtime is a workstation you can lose, which is why the credential storage choice is in the rootfs.
